newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to forecast most on track for EMU - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: EU to forecast most on track for EMU - newspaper.

text.p: The European Commission's next economic forecasts for the European Union will indicate that at least 10 and possibly 14 countries will be ready for the single currency in 1999, The European Voice newspaper said on Friday.

The newspaper, a Brussels-based weekly, said forecasts due for release on November 6 would paint a rosy picture compared with the last report in May when the Commission saw 1996 growth at 1.5 percent.
It would now be higher than this, the newspaper said, citing Commission economists as sources. But the prediction of 2.4-percent growth in 1997 was unlikely to change, it said.
Improved economic fortunes in Germany were the main motor, it said, with the Commission seeing German GDP rising above one percent this year and two percent in 1997.
This growth will mean Germany will remain on track to have a deficit of less than three percent of GDP in 1997, one of the key Maastricht criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU)
The Commission is also expected to stick with its prediction that France's deficit will fall below the three-percent of GDP threshhold.

"Alongside these two key players in the euro zone, the Commission will predict that at least eight more member states -- the Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark, Luxembourg, Ireland, Austria, Finland and Sweden -- are on course to meet the three-percent target for 1997," the newspaper said.
With a little more budgetary austerity, Spain, Portugal and Britain could join the group.
It said Commission officials were still pouring over Italy's proposed austerity programme to see whether they should cut their deficit forecast of 5.2 percent of GDP.
